input.quote: 15. ASSIGNMENT OR TRANSFER. Neither party shall assign or transfer any of its rights under this Agreement without the prior written approval of the other party, except no such approval shall be required for an assignment to a financially responsible affiliate.
input.rationale: Section 15 is the only assignment provision in the Agreement (no change-of-control or deemed-assignment language appears anywhere, and neither the term nor termination provisions in Sections 13-14 give TrueLink any right triggered by our change of control). The clause is mutual and carves out affiliate assignments, but it fails the fallback on two material terms: there is no carve-out permitting assignment to a successor in a merger or sale of substantially all assets (M&A transfers require TrueLink's approval), and the consent requirement carries no reasonableness standard, so TrueLink could withhold approval arbitrarily. We therefore edited Section 15 to the fallback: a mutual successor carve-out on written notice, with consent for other assignments not to be unreasonably withheld. We did not pursue the preferred asymmetric position (Vendor consent, no assignment to a competitor) because the fallback is met by a single conforming edit.

proposal.summary: Add mutual successor carve-out on written notice and a reasonableness standard to the consent requirement.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have added a mutual carve-out permitting assignment to a successor in a merger or sale of substantially all assets on written notice, and made the consent required for other assignments subject to a reasonableness standard. This is our fallback assignment position; the existing affiliate carve-out is unchanged.

ops.oldText: Neither party shall assign or transfer any of its rights under this Agreement without the prior written approval of the other party, except no such approval shall be required for an assignment to a financially responsible affiliate.
ops.newText: Neither party shall assign or transfer its rights under this Agreement without the prior written approval of the other party, which shall not be unreasonably withheld, except no approval is required for assignment to a financially responsible affiliate or, upon written notice, to a successor in a merger or sale of substantially all assets.
